proposals.before: His father Mu was a commandery clerk.
proposals.after: His father Mu was a provincial clerk (zhou zhubu).
proposals.reason: 州主簿 is a provincial (zhou) clerk, not a commandery office.

proposals.before: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru, the minister Yuan Xian, and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, and also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.
proposals.after: Xian successively memorialized and impeached Minister of Works Sima Ziru, the minister Yuan Xian, and Administrator of Yong province Murong Xian, and also impeached Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Tan and inspector of Bing province Kezhuhun Daoyuan—the charges written to the utmost; all were removed from office.
proposals.reason: 咸陽王坦 is Prince of Xianyang named Tan; 王 is the title 'prince', not the surname Wang.

proposals.before: On the sixth day he required Wei grand tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and the rest to assemble, brought them into the Northern Palace, and kept them in the eastern study — only after the abdication were they released to their homes.
proposals.after: On the sixth day he required Wei grand tutor Prince of Xianyang Tan and the rest to assemble, brought them into the Northern Palace, and kept them in the eastern study — only after the abdication were they released to their homes.
proposals.reason: Same error: 咸陽王坦 is Tan, Prince of Xianyang, not Wang Tan.

proposals.before: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu with grand master of ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, palace attendant Zhang Liang, and yellow gate Zhao Yanshen to report at court.
proposals.after: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Xu with grand master of ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, palace attendant Zhang Liang, and yellow gate Zhao Yanshen to report at court.
proposals.reason: 襄城王旭 is Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng; 王 is the title, not surname Wang.

proposals.before: Gao Yang later regretted it; Dezheng was posthumously made grand guardian; his eldest grandson's son Wangchen inherited the title.
proposals.after: Gao Yang later regretted it; Dezheng was posthumously made grand guardian; his eldest grandson Wangchen inherited the title.
proposals.reason: 嫡孫 means eldest grandson, not great-grandson ('eldest grandson's son').

proposals.before: The Wei emperor asked vice director Cui Xuan, minister Yang Yin, and others, "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how often? Tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."
proposals.after: The Wei emperor asked vice director Cui Xian, minister Yang Yin, and others, "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how often? Tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."
proposals.reason: 崔暹 is Cui Xian throughout this chapter; 'Cui Xuan' is a wrong referent.

proposals.before: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though at rest, never cease to rest."
proposals.after: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though blessed with auspicious signs, not rest on them."
proposals.reason: 雖休勿休 means do not grow complacent because of favorable omens; the current English is opaque.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Wuding, he was moved to chief inspector; he selected Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei, Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang as inspectors—men of the age called this knowing men.
proposals.after: At the beginning of Wuding, he was moved to chief inspector; he selected Bi Yiyun, Lu Qian, Song Qindao, Li Yin, Cui Zhan, Du Rui, Ji Ye, Li Bowei (酈伯偉), Cui Ziwu, and Li Guang as inspectors—men of the age called this knowing men.
proposals.reason: The Chinese surname is 酈, distinct from 李 used for Li Yin and Li Guang; mark the character to avoid conflation.

decisions.after: His father Mu was a provincial clerk.
decisions.reason: s0003 has 州主簿, a zhou-level office, so 'commandery clerk' is wrong; drop the parenthetical gloss and keep natural idiomatic English as 'provincial clerk'.
s0026 has 太師咸陽王坦; 王 is the princely title in 咸陽王, and 坦 is the personal name, so 'Wang Tan' falsely invents the surname Wang.
s0127 has 魏太傅咸陽王坦; again 王 belongs to the title 咸陽王 and the name is 坦, so removing the false surname Wang is required.
s0133 has 魏襄城王旭; 王 is the title in 襄城王 and 旭 is the personal name, so 'Wang Xu' wrongly treats 王 as a surname.
s0178 has 嫡孫王臣; 嫡孫 means the eldest/heir grandson, not a great-grandson phrased as 'eldest grandson's son'.
s0191 names 僕射崔暹; this chapter's subject is Cui Xian (崔暹), so 'Cui Xuan' is a wrong referent and Cui Xian restores the supported name.
s0194 closes Ang's omen speech with 雖休勿休; in this sweet-dew context it warns against complacency on auspicious signs, and the opaque 'never cease to rest' misreads 休.
s0019's 酈伯偉 is already rendered Li Bowei; inserting the Chinese characters into English prose is a stylistic annotation, not a semantic repair of an inaccurate translation.
